prespecification_note: Written and checksum-pinned before any model prediction was computed in code. Not blinded: the observed group means (AUC, CL/F, fraction excreted unchanged) were read before writing this plan, and a rough mental calculation suggested that scaling renal clearance in proportion to creatinine clearance (reading A) may over-predict renal clearance in the moderate group. This is disclosed here; the readings and the classification rule were fixed regardless.
not_this: Not validation; group means only, small groups (5-7 subjects).
Not a full PBPK model: no organ volumes, tissue partitioning or transporter kinetics are used.
Not a dosing or exposure prediction for any patient.
question: Calibrated only on the normal-renal-function group, does a model that splits lenalidomide elimination into filtration, tubular secretion and non-renal pathways predict exposure and urinary excretion in mild, moderate and severe renal impairment; and does secretion scale with creatinine clearance (intact nephron) or stay constant?

data.evidence: intelligence_store/data/lenalidomide_renal_pathways_evidence_v1.json (EMA 2008, study CC-5013-PK-001, single 25 mg oral dose, fasting)

calibration_normal_group_only.total_clearance: CL_n = dose / mean AUC_n (ratio of means), expressed in mL/min. This is CL/F; bioavailability is taken as 1 (at least about 0.85 from urinary recovery).
calibration_normal_group_only.renal_clearance: CLR_n = fe_n x CL_n, with fe_n the mean fraction of dose excreted unchanged (0.85). CLR = Ae / AUC does not depend on bioavailability.
calibration_normal_group_only.non_renal_clearance: CLNR = CL_n - CLR_n, held constant across renal function.
calibration_normal_group_only.unbound_fraction: fu = 0.77 (binding 23% in myeloma plasma); sensitivity fu = 0.71 (healthy volunteers).
calibration_normal_group_only.filtration_and_secretion: Filtration_n = fu x CrCl_n; Secretion_n = CLR_n - Filtration_n (must be positive; otherwise reported as inconsistent with net secretion).

readings.A_intact_nephron: Filtration and secretion both fall in proportion to creatinine clearance: CLR = CLR_n x CrCl / CrCl_n.
readings.B_secretion_preserved: Filtration falls in proportion to creatinine clearance; secretion stays at Secretion_n: CLR = fu x CrCl + Secretion_n.

predictions: For each impaired group and reading: CL = CLR + CLNR; AUC = dose / CL; fe = CLR / CL.

creatinine_clearance_scenarios.why: Group creatinine clearance values are reported only as ranges; the same ranges as the earlier Hughes and Kim renal-group checks are used.

sensitivity.label: impaired groups at their upper limits
impaired groups at their lower limits

endpoints.primary: Mean AUC of each impaired group (mild, moderate, severe without dialysis).
descriptive: fraction of dose excreted unchanged (fe; no SD reported, so not classified)
predicted split of clearance into filtration, secretion and non-renal pathways

comparison.interval: 95% confidence interval of the observed mean AUC: mean +/- t(0.975, n - 1) x SD / sqrt(n).

decision_rule.supported: A reading is called supported if its primary-scenario AUC is consistent for all three impaired groups.
decision_rule.finding_if_steeper_decline: If reading A under-predicts AUC in the moderate or severe group in the primary scenario, record as a finding that renal elimination falls faster than proportional scaling with creatinine clearance predicts.
decision_rule.never: No parameter is fitted to the impaired groups. Calibration uses the normal group and the binding value only.

known_differences: Creatinine clearance was measured, but each group is summarised only by a range; representative values are assumptions.
Measured creatinine clearance overestimates GFR because creatinine is also secreted; filtration is therefore approximate.
Means of small groups; the observed fe has no reported spread.
Single dose, fasting; healthy and patient subjects not distinguished in the source pages.
